answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a refundable identity bond verified by a rotating panel of peers before any newcomer may trade or vote. Every fake identity needs its own locked deposit, so a hundred clones require a hundred bonds; any duplicate the panel catches is slashed and barred, so expected cost equals bond size times clone count times detection chance. Trust grows on that collateral like coral on a reef, lifting honest agents toward the zenith of the ranking, while a fraudster's claims fall to a whisper once its stake is burned.
